title: Antigravity Masters Class
description: Full Antigravity mastery: agent briefs, workspace context, multi-step missions, review discipline, session systems, and team-ready AI development habits.

lessons.title: Antigravity as an Agent Workspace

introduction.text: Antigravity is built for agentic coding: the environment carries project context so agents can propose edits with awareness of your files and goals. Your job is to define missions, constrain blast radius, and enforce review. Chatbots answer; agents attempt work—you still approve.

questions.correctAnswer: Acting on tasks in your workspace with context

options: How much of the system a change can affect
questions.correctAnswer: How much of the system a change can affect

questions.question: Project context improves agents by:
options: Grounding actions in real files and conventions
questions.correctAnswer: Grounding actions in real files and conventions

lessons.title: Writing Agent Briefs that Ship

introduction.text: A strong agent brief has: objective, non-goals, acceptance tests, allowed files, reference examples, and definition of done. Include “stop and ask” conditions. Prefer checkable outcomes over vibes. Briefs are the product spec for autonomous work.

lessons.title: Context Engineering for Agents

introduction.text: Feed the smallest sufficient context: interfaces, failing tests, error logs, and adjacent modules—not the whole monorepo. Maintain a living “project card” (stack, commands, conventions). Refresh context when the agent drifts.

options: Only what is needed to act correctly
questions.correctAnswer: Only what is needed to act correctly

When an agent drifts you should:

lessons.title: Multi-Step Missions and Orchestration

introduction.text: Break epics into missions with dependencies: spike → implement → test → polish. Run one mission at a time unless you have isolation. Require artifacts at each gate (plan.md, diff, test output). Parallelize only independent workstreams.

lessons.title: Review Discipline: Diffs, Risks, Rollbacks

introduction.text: Read every agent diff like a PR from a new teammate. Check intent vs brief, security, data handling, and test gaps. Require agents to summarize risk and rollback. Reject “drive-by” refactors. Keep an allowlist of auto-apply for trivial edits only.
